_comment: The clock and rate figures are the 90 MHz nominal. The amplitude, crosstalk and silent-level values date from 2026-08-22 at 78 MHz on another board, and are old references until re-derived. A record of one board, not a
datasheet: re-measure rather than re-derive if any of it is in doubt.
Tolerances come from the observed run-to-run spread. A tolerance
tighter than the spread is a flaky test; one much looser is not a test.
The DAC span and ADVREF used to live here and now live in
calibration.json at the repository root, read through
host/calibration.py. They are measurements of the hardware,
not expectations about its behaviour, and four things
outside tests/ were reaching in here to get them.
lib/due_shared/src/fw_version.h, which both tracks compile.
It used to be two hand-copied files and the string drifted from
the numbers; the string is derived now. Bump both together: a
board reporting a version this file does not know about is
either a stale flash or an un-updated baseline, and the test
cannot tell you which if only one of them moved.
Floors, not bands. Measured five 4 s runs per mode on this board:
in-dma 19.8-30.5, out-dma 17.9-28.2, duplex-dma 8.2-20.0 MB/s, a
run-to-run spread of 35-59%. That is far wider than the ~5% this
project's notes previously recorded, so a floor near the typical
figure is a flaky test, not a strict one. What these have to catch
is a collapse - the ~1.7 MB/s gated-OUT regime that once blocked
full-rate duplex - and they still catch it by a factor of three or
more.

transport_measured_mbs._comment: Observed range, five 4 s runs per mode, 2026-08-22.

_comment: Underruns tolerated per ladder run.
Zero is the requirement and nothing else is acceptable in the end.
But host-fed playback sporadically underruns at rates that are
otherwise clean - 2 and 3 in a both-track run at RC 86 and RC 50,
which pass 5/5 on their own - while the rates that genuinely
starve give 15 to 50. A tolerance of 5 separates that tail from a
real collapse, so the ladders stay usable as a regression gate
instead of failing at random.
This used to say to remove it when objective 0 closed. Objective 0
was the lost-sample defect and it has closed, but this is not its
tail: an underrun is the ring running dry, not data going missing.
It belongs to the feed policy in objective 0a, which is open.
Whether it is still needed has not been retested since the fix -
measure before removing it.
Main-loop load, measured on THIS board with the cycle-counter
monitor (bsp/load.c). Idle and steady-state capture both put
essentially every pass in one log2 bucket, which is what makes
an outlier meaningful. Floors are well below the measured rate
because the point is to catch a loop that has stopped running,
not to police a few per cent of drift.
The idle pass went 9.72 -> 7.90 -> 6.70 us as ctl_service and then
usb_cdc_poll were gated to 1 kHz. Both were reading a UOTGHS
register every pass to ask about events that happen tens of times
a second. load_tick itself is free at this resolution: 128.1 k with
it against 127.4 k built out. Re-measure rather than scale.
These are Track B's. The monitor is shared from 2026-08-28 and
the suite runs on both tracks; the floors are loose enough to
cover both, but the loops are NOT the same. Track A idles at
75.1 k passes/s against Track B's 160.4 k on this bench - a 2.14x
difference that is its own finding, open in issue #13. Do not
read a Track A number against idle_passes_per_s below.

dc_transfer._comment: DC transfer fit in A0 codes against DAC code, Track B, 90 MHz, 2026-10-31. Five kept repeats per ADC rate (rc_for(200000)=225 and RC 86), repeat 0 of each dropped by index. slope_ref and offset_ref: mean of all ten kept. slope_tol and offset_tol: 5x the larger per-rate standard deviation (2.4e-5 and 0.073), above the between-rate difference (6e-5 and 0.16), rounded up. resid_max_codes: floor of 3 over 2x the worst kept residual (0.45). physics_tol is a provisional bound (check) pending phase G and the datasheet. A whole run can sit 2-3 codes off at any one level (a constant shift of the whole settled window, not a settling tail: 4 of 60 level readings in 12 forward sweeps, the largest -3.2 codes, mechanism not established), so the gate must pass one level 3.2 codes off. Such a level moves the slope by up to 0.00072 and the offset by up to 2.1 codes, and its own residual reaches 2.56 codes at the middle level; added to the across-session range of slope (0.67008-0.67044) and offset (674.0-674.7) that gives slope_tol 0.001, offset_tol 2.7 and resid_max_codes 4. A level shifted by 8 codes still fails: by the residual (5.1 or more) at the middle levels, and at the end levels, where the residual is 3.6, by the slope, which it moves by 0.0018. Provisional until phase G re-derives all of it from more sessions. TWO-BOARD WIDENING, 2026-11-06, PRE-CALIBRATION: the figures above are board ...3030363139303038 (offset 674.4, slope 0.6703). A second Due, ...3030393033313035 at 7ccc732, measured offset 682.5 and slope 0.66958 (rms 0.15 codes, two sessions, both ADC rates). slope_ref and offset_ref are now the midpoints, rounded (0.67 and 678.5); offset_tol is the half-gap 4.05 plus twice the old 2.7 allowance. slope_tol is 0.0013, not the 0.0015 asked for: tests/test_dc_fit.py holds that an 8-code level shift at an end level and a 6-code shift at 512 still fail, and 0.0014 already breaks that, so 0.0013 is the widest value the guards allow (half-gap 0.0004 plus the 0.00072 allowance for a 3.2-code level is 0.0011). Owner-approved to pass both boards before per-board calibration exists; it is not a derived spread. Replace with per-board gates.

noise._comment: Held-code noise on A0, code 2048 on DAC0, noise-fast capture (tools/noise_metrics.py), linux-x1, 90 MHz, build d7ece10. Rule, mechanical: rms_ceiling_lsb is the largest rms_lsb over every kept row (run != 0, no error) of the ten records/g-*-noise-fast.jsonl sets (six in place, four reflash; Tracks A, B, C at RC 86 and 225), 0.8976, times 1.15, rounded up to 2 decimals. line_fraction_ceiling is the largest split.line_power_fraction over the same rows, 0.0410, times 1.15, rounded up to 2 decimals; n_lines is 0 in some rows and 1 in others, so the bound is on the line's power fraction, not on n_lines == 0. The floor check needs no number here: a reading below 0.9 of the row's own quantisation_floor_lsb (0.2887 codes) is a flat or stale capture. Provisional (check) until more sessions and benches; one bench so far, and a board with excess noise would be rejected only above this bound.
noise._probes_extra_comment: Extra room for a bench that declares probes on (bench.json "probes": "on"); tests/helpers.py apply_probe_state adds it to the probes-off bound and does nothing otherwise. Rule: worst probes-on value over the 84 kept rows of records/station-repeat-montreal5.jsonl (board ...3030363139303038, Track B, 90 MHz, RC 86 and 225, 2026-11-06; labels seat0-asis, seat1-4, probes-back, late-asis; first run of each set dropped by index) minus the probes-off bound above, times 1.05, rounded up to 2 decimals. Probes-off bounds are not changed by this. One board, one day; Tracks A and C were not used to derive it.

sinad._comment: SINAD, THD and ENOB of a coherent sine in the DAC->ADC loop (tools/noise_metrics.py sinad_once), linux-x1, 90 MHz, build bf8af90. Source: the nine records/h-<track>-<rc>-<ip|rf>-sinad.jsonl sets (Tracks A, B, C x in-place RC 225, in-place RC 86, reflash RC 225), 69 kept rows (run != 0, no error). Rule, mechanical (derived by a script, not by eye): per key, drop rows more than 4 median absolute deviations from their own set's median (set-wise; no exclusion in a set whose MAD is 0), leaving the bulk; bound = bulk extreme extended outward by the bulk range (max - min over all bulk rows), floored or ceilinged at 2 decimals. Excluded per key: sinad_db 5, enob 5, thd_db 6, noise_floor_rms_lsb 5, signal_rms_lsb 10. The bulk drops one spike row (a-225-ip: floor 5.97 codes, SINAD 44.23) and a bound from the extreme including it would be useless, so the test confirms a failure with one fresh measurement instead (helpers.confirm_measurement). The signal band is narrow because the amplitude is set by the DAC and the host, not by noise. Provisional (check) until more sessions and benches. TWO-BOARD WIDENING, 2026-11-06, PRE-CALIBRATION: sinad_db_min 59.85 to 59.0, enob_min 9.65 to 9.5 and noise_floor_rms_lsb_max 0.97 to 1.1 only. Board ...3030393033313035 at 7ccc732 measured SINAD 59.78 dB and noise floor 0.977 codes at RC 225, just past the bounds derived on ...3030363139303038; the new bounds are owner-approved and are not a derived spread. Replace with per-board gates. signal_rms_lsb is the exception to the exclusion: it has no spike population, only ordinary spread, so the MAD rule threw out 10 of 69 good rows and left a 1.06-code band that two kept rows (968.94 and 971.77) already fell outside; its band is the extreme over ALL 69 kept rows (968.94 to 971.77) extended by their range (2.83): 966.11 to 974.6.
sinad._probes_extra_comment: Extra room for a bench that declares probes on (bench.json "probes": "on"); tests/helpers.py apply_probe_state adds it to the probes-off bound and does nothing otherwise. Rule: worst probes-on value over the 84 kept rows of records/station-repeat-montreal5.jsonl (board ...3030363139303038, Track B, 90 MHz, RC 86 and 225, 2026-11-06; labels seat0-asis, seat1-4, probes-back, late-asis; first run of each set dropped by index) minus the probes-off bound above, times 1.05, rounded up to 2 decimals. Probes-off bounds are not changed by this. One board, one day; Tracks A and C were not used to derive it.

tone_sweep._comment: Amplitude on A0 and crosstalk on A1 against tone (tools/metrics.py tone_sweep_once; N samples per cycle, N = 256, 64, 16, 8), linux-x1, 90 MHz, build bf8af90. Source: the nine records/h-<track>-<rc>-<ip|rf>-tone-sweep.jsonl sets (Tracks A, B, C x in-place RC 225, in-place RC 86, reflash RC 225), 69 kept rows (run != 0, no error). Rule, mechanical (script derive_tone.py, not by eye): per key, drop rows more than 4 median absolute deviations from their own set's median (set-wise; no exclusion in a set whose MAD is 0), leaving the bulk; bound = bulk extreme extended outward by the bulk range, floored (minimums) or ceilinged (maximums) at 2 decimals. If the exclusion would remove more than 15% of the 69 rows for a key, no row is excluded for that key and the bound comes from all 69. Rows the rule would drop / used: amp_n256 would drop 12, none excluded; amp_n64 would drop 12, none excluded; amp_n16 9 excluded; amp_n8 would drop 11, none excluded; xtalk_n256 7 excluded; xtalk_n64 10 excluded; xtalk_n16 would drop 12, none excluded. xtalk_max_n8 is the maximum over all 69 kept rows (4.40) times 1.15, ceilinged at 2 decimals: spikes of 2.5-4.4 occur on all three tracks (4 of 23 rows on Track A), too many to exclude, so it is a catastrophe detector only. amp_n8_frac dips to 0 in some rows and is not gated; frac_min applies to N = 256, 64, 16. The amp_n16 band is narrow because its 9 excluded rows hold all the spread; a failure is confirmed by one fresh measurement (helpers.confirm_measurement). Provisional (check) until more sessions and benches. TWO-BOARD WIDENING, 2026-11-06, PRE-CALIBRATION: amp_min_n16 and amp_max_n16 only. The old band 1371.22-1372.66 is board ...3030363139303038; ...3030393033313035 reads 1370.3-1370.6 (7ccc732). The band is rounded outward to 1365-1375 from the two boards' envelope, owner-approved, not derived from a spread. Replace with per-board gates.

loop_skew._comment: The A1-after-A0 lag of one sine in the matched loop (tools/metrics.py loop_skew_once), linux-x1, 90 MHz, build bf8af90. One figure: DAC1-after-DAC0 lag plus the A1-before-A0 spacing; they are not separable. Source: the nine records/h-<track>-<rc>-<ip|rf>-loop-skew.jsonl sets (Tracks A, B, C x in-place RC 225, in-place RC 86, reflash RC 225), 69 kept rows (run != 0, no error); derived by a scratchpad script, numbers re-taken from the records. The lag is an integer multiple k of the trigger period 1/fs: k = 1 in 52 rows, k = 2 in 17, on every track and at both rates. k varies between runs and across a reflash, cause not established, so k_allowed is [1, 2] and no gate may assume k = 1. deviation_ns_max 25 is the smallest round number above 17.99 ns, the largest deviation from k/fs among the 63 rows outside the six that exceed it (six of 69 rows exceed 25 ns, up to 666 ns, two of them half-way rows), which is why a failure is confirmed by one fresh measurement (helpers.confirm_measurement). phase_sd_deg_max is the maximum over all 69 rows (0.0021555) times 1.15, rounded up to 5 decimals. Provisional (check) until more sessions and benches.

square_shape._comment: The 100 kHz and 400 kHz full-amplitude square in the DAC0->A0 loop (tools/square_shape.py square_gate_once), linux-x1, 90 MHz, build 0847604, default DAC bias (2,1). Source: the six records/sq-<track>-<ip|rf>-square-gate.jsonl sets (Tracks A, B, C x in-place, reflash); derived by a scratchpad script from the records: 48 rows with run != 0 and no error (the brief expected 60 and the bounds below agree with its figures, so the count is the only difference). Rise and fall are bimodal one 22.2 ns tick apart (277 or 300 ns rise) and the mode moves on reflash, so rise_ns_*_max and fall_ns_*_max are the bulk maximum (300.92, 300.64, 303.26, 302.96) plus the bulk range (23.94, 23.93, 23.65, 23.62), which tolerates both modes with one tick of headroom. vpp_frac_400k_min 0.99 is the 400 kHz swing over the 100 kHz swing: bulk 0.99722-0.99746, chosen 1% below because the range rule would sit only 3e-4 under the data; bias 0 reads 0.957. flat_*_min are 0.9 x the bulk minimum (0.71429 at 400 kHz; 0.92857 hi and 0.91964 lo at 100 kHz): the bulk range is 0 or 0.009, so the rule gives no margin and the 10% is a chosen margin, not a derived one. Bias 0 reads rise 838 ns and flat 0.07 at 400 kHz. No gate on vpp_codes_100k: gain is the DC test's job. Provisional (check) until more sessions, benches and builds.
